builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
summary: WildAWM replaces reliance on human-collected computer-use trajectories and hand-built training environments with an open-source-model pipeline that synthesizes executable GUI/MCP/CLI environments, tasks, and execution-based verifiers. It costs a full environment-generation and agent-training workflow: heterogeneous rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, counterfactual probes, and fine-tuning runs, which is feasible with open models but exceeds casual experimentation on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail if synthetic tasks drift from real-world distributions, if verifiers reward incorrect trajectories that pass the quality gates, or if gains do not transfer to the reader's specific target applications.
rationale: The pipeline is open-source and runs on open models, so a small team can trial environment synthesis at reduced scale, but the end-to-end generation, verification, and training loop requires workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Synthetic environment synthesis for computer-use agent training

claims.statement: WildAWM replaces reliance on human-collected computer-use trajectories and hand-built training environments with an open-source-model pipeline that synthesizes executable GUI/MCP/CLI environments, tasks, and execution-based verifiers. It costs a full environment-generation and agent-training workflow: heterogeneous rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, counterfactual probes, and fine-tuning runs, which is feasible with open models but exceeds casual experimentation on a single 24 GB GPU. It can fail if synthetic tasks drift from real-world distributions, if verifiers reward incorrect trajectories that pass the quality gates, or if gains do not transfer to the reader's specific target applications.
Qwen models trained exclusively on 341 synthesized environment-task pairs show substantial gains on 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks; tasks remain difficult, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60%.
